## 1. System Overview & Architectural Invariants

B.L.A.S.T. is an enterprise, self-hosted, deterministic document intelligence and OCR engine designed for high-throughput batch execution and Agentic RAG ingestion. It solves three critical failure modes of conventional document processing pipelines:

1. **Slow CPU Inference Latency**: Solved via ONNX Runtime execution (RapidOCR/PP-OCRv4) with automatic multi-provider fallback (`CUDA` → `DirectML` → `CPU`), cutting CPU per-page latency from ~117.8s to ~15.3s (7.7x faster) and reducing mean CER by 18% versus an EasyOCR/PyTorch baseline on the project's 14-page gold corpus (ADR 0005).
2. **Memory Accumulation & Unbounded OOM Crashes**: Solved via a bounded sliding-window memory buffer streaming architecture (`StreamingPDFProcessor`); verified across a 1,000-page continuous streaming stress test measuring a linear growth slope of 0.0002 MB/page against a 0.005 MB/page zero-leak threshold (`eval/results/stress_report.json`).
3. **Loss of Document Semantics & Generative Hallucination**: Solved via deterministic morphological table grid extraction (scored with a built-in TEDS evaluator), LaTeX math expression detection ($...$, $$...$$), running header/footer suppression, and dual-layer sandwich PDF generation with exact word-level coordinate bounding box alignment. Zero generative hallucination in legal, compliance, and financial records.

### Architectural Philosophy: The 3-Layer A.N.T. Paradigm
- **Layer 1: Architect (Protocols & Schemas)**: Static rules of engagement, data schemas, priority policies, error code taxonomies (`architecture/`, `GEMINI.md`).
- **Layer 2: Navigator (Router & Pipeline Supervisor)**: Dynamic state management, job lifecycle, batch sizing, multi-format export orchestration (`blast_ocr/pipeline.py`).
- **Layer 3: Tools (Deterministic Atomic Execution)**: Pure, isolated worker modules in `blast_ocr/core/` (extractor, table reconstruction, formula parsing, PII masking, SIMD pre-processing).

## 2. Product Marketing & Persona Context

### Target Audience & Core ICP
- **Teams**: AI/ML Engineering teams, Legal Tech platforms, Financial Services & Compliance, Archival/Publishing Institutions, Healthcare/Life Sciences.
- **Decision-Makers**: Head of AI/ML, Lead AI Engineer, VP of Engineering, CTO, Senior Data Platform Architect, Security & Compliance Officer.
- **Primary Use Case**: Ingesting high-volume, multi-format document archives (1,000+ pages) into structured RAG pipelines and searchable databases without memory leaks, cloud API bills, or data privacy risks.

### Persona Matrix
| Persona | Primary Focus | Core Frustration | B.L.A.S.T. Value Proposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AI / RAG Engineer** | Output Markdown fidelity, token efficiency, hierarchy preservation, vector search | Scanned documents produce unstructured "word soup", broken tables, and bloated tokens | Clean GFM Markdown with preserved KaTeX formulas ($...$, $$...$$), GFM tables, native LangChain/LlamaIndex loaders |
| **Platform / Backend Engineer** | Memory stability, CPU/GPU latency, horizontal scaling, Docker deployment | PyTorch OCR engines leak memory, crash worker nodes with OOM, take >100s per page | ONNX multi-provider fallback (7.7x faster than EasyOCR), 0.0002 MB/page streaming leak slope, 3-tier Redis priority queue, zombie reaper |
| **VP of Engineering / CTO** | Development velocity, compute costs, deterministic reliability, license safety | Cloud OCR APIs (AWS Textract, Google Document AI) create massive monthly cloud bills and vendor lock-in | 100% MIT-licensed, completely self-hosted, zero per-page fees, reproducible benchmarks |
| **Security & Compliance Officer** | Data sovereignty, zero telemetry, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, PII protection | Sending confidential client contracts, patient records, or financial disclosures to cloud APIs violates compliance | 100% offline, local execution with zero network transit, strict sandboxing against path traversal/XXE, and automated 8-class forensic PII redaction |

## 3. Quantitative Performance Benchmarks & Competitor Comparison

### 3.1 In-Repo Engine Bake-Off (14-Page Gold Corpus, Reproducible via `python -m eval.run`)

| Metric | RapidOCR (Default) | EasyOCR (Previous) | Phase-0 (Tesseract-Backed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mean Character Error Rate (CER)** | **0.1916** | 0.2338 | 0.4992 |
| **Mean Word Error Rate (WER)** | **0.4739** | 0.4968 | 0.7288 |
| **Reading Order Tau Correlation** | **0.9758** | 0.9641 | n/a |
| **Avg. CPU Latency/Page** | **~15.3s** | ~117.8s | n/a |

### 3.2 Comprehensive Feature Matrix

| Feature | B.L.A.S.T. OCR | IBM Docling | Marker 2 | Tesseract | AWS Textract |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Dual-Layer Searchable PDF** | **Native PyMuPDF** | No | No | Basic PDF | Extra cost |
| **LaTeX Math Recognition** | **Built-in ($...$, $$...$$)** | Partial | Yes | No | No |
| **Native AI Agent MCP Server** | **Built-in (stdio/SSE)** | No | No | No | No |
| **Streaming Memory Stability** | **0.0002 MB/page slope** | Unbounded | High VRAM | Moderate | Cloud API |
| **Generative Hallucination Risk**| **0% (Deterministic)** | Low | Low | 0% | Cloud |
| **License Terms** | **MIT (100% Permissive)** | MIT | GPL-3.0 + OpenRAIL-M | Apache-2.0 | Proprietary SaaS |
| **Runs 100% Offline** | **Yes (Zero Telemetry)** | Yes | Yes | Yes | No (Cloud only) |

## 4. Complete Python SDK API Reference

### 4.1 In-Process Synchronous Pipeline
```python
from blast_ocr.pipeline import OCRPipeline

# Initialize deterministic pipeline
pipeline = OCRPipeline(
    engine="rapidocr",       # Options: "rapidocr" (default), "easyocr", "tesseract", "ensemble"
    secure_mode=True,        # Enables automated 8-class forensic PII redaction
    batch_size=16            # Vectorized SIMD batch slice
)

# Process PDF document to multiple formats simultaneously
result = pipeline.process(
    source_path="document.pdf",
    output_dir="outputs/",
    formats=["markdown", "docx", "pdf", "epub", "json"]
)

print(f"Status: {result['status']}")
print(f"Extracted Text:\n{result['text']}")
print(f"Generated Files: {result['generated_files']}")
```

### 4.2 Streaming Processing for 1,000+ Page Archives
```python
from blast_ocr.core.streaming import StreamingPDFProcessor

processor = StreamingPDFProcessor(
    window_size=10,          # Sliding window chunk limit
    scratch_dir=".tmp/scratch"
)

for chunk in processor.stream_pages("massive_archive.pdf"):
    print(f"Processed pages {chunk.start_page} to {chunk.end_page}")
    # Process or persist chunk without accumulating full document in memory
```

---

## 5. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server

AI agents in Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Devin, and Antigravity connect via native stdio:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "blast-ocr": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["-m", "blast_ocr.mcp_server"],
      "env": {
        "BLAST_OCR_ENGINE": "rapidocr"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Exposed MCP Tools:
- `blast_ocr_process`: Complete document OCR extraction with multi-format generation (Markdown, PDF, DOCX, JSON).
- `blast_ocr_extract_tables`: Morphological table detection and cell reconstruction into Markdown and HTML.
- `blast_ocr_extract_formulas`: Mathematical formula recognition into KaTeX Markdown.
- `blast_ocr_semantic_chunk`: Hierarchy-aware document chunking for agentic RAG retrieval.

---

## 6. AI Agent Integration Recipes (LangChain & LlamaIndex)

### LangChain Document Loader
```python
from blast_ocr.integrations import BlastOCRDocumentLoader

loader = BlastOCRDocumentLoader(
    file_path="quarterly_earnings.pdf",
    extract_tables=True,
    extract_formulas=True
)
docs = loader.load()
```

### LlamaIndex Reader
```python
from blast_ocr.integrations import BlastOCRReader
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex

documents = BlastOCRReader().load_data(file_path="whitepaper.pdf")
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
```

---

## 7. Command Line Interface (CLI)

```bash
# High-speed document processing with dual-layer PDF export
python run.py document.pdf --formats md,docx,pdf --out results/

# Process batch directory
python run.py /path/to/batch/ --formats md,txt --out results/

# Scanned book processing with spine curvature dewarping
python run.py thick_book.pdf --dewarp --engine ensemble --out book_results/

# Launch Enterprise REST API server
python run.py --serve --port 8000

# Launch Sovereign Streamlit Mission Control GUI
streamlit run blast_ocr/ui/web_app.py
```

## Competitor Comparisons & Modern Alternatives
- [B.L.A.S.T. vs Tesseract OCR](docs/comparisons/blast-vs-tesseract.md): 16x faster CPU execution, table recovery, 0.9758 reading order vs legacy connected-components.
- [B.L.A.S.T. vs EasyOCR](docs/comparisons/blast-vs-easyocr.md): 7.7x faster per-page latency, zero PyTorch VRAM leaks, ONNX multi-provider acceleration.
- [B.L.A.S.T. vs AWS Textract](docs/comparisons/blast-vs-aws-textract.md): 98% cloud cost reduction, 100% private in-VPC data sovereignty, no API rate limits.
- [B.L.A.S.T. vs IBM Docling](docs/comparisons/blast-vs-docling.md): Lightweight 15MB ONNX weights vs 1.5GB PyTorch transformer models, native MCP server.
- [B.L.A.S.T. vs Marker 2](docs/comparisons/blast-vs-marker.md): Permissive MIT license vs GPL-3.0/OpenRAIL commercial caps, CPU-native execution.
- [Best Tesseract Alternative (2026 Guide)](docs/comparisons/tesseract-alternative.md): 60-second migration guide eliminating OS package dependencies.
- [Best Self-Hosted AWS Textract Alternative](docs/comparisons/aws-textract-alternative.md): Enterprise blueprint for private in-VPC OCR migration.
